title: fix(app-shell): the console dashboard refreshes on its authored refreshIntervalSeconds (objectui#11062)
body:
Fixes #11062
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`DashboardView` rendered `DashboardRenderer` with no `onRefresh`, and `useDashboardAutoRefresh` arms its interval only when a host wires one, so an authored `refreshIntervalSeconds` never started a timer in the console.

`DashboardView` now passes `onRefresh={refreshDashboardData}`, a module-level function that calls `notifyDataChanged({ objectName: '*' })` from `@object-ui/react`. There is no second timer: the hook still owns the interval, and the handler only declares one unscoped change on the data-invalidation bus. The widgets that hold a bus subscription re-read in place. Nothing re-keys, remounts or re-derives the schema, and there is no `useCallback`: the hook reads the handler through a ref (objectui#11004), and a module-level function has a stable identity anyway.

Files: `packages/app-shell/src/views/DashboardView.tsx`, a new pin `packages/app-shell/src/views/DashboardView.autoRefresh-11062.test.tsx`, the app-shell README, `content/docs/guide/console.md`, and `.changeset/11062-console-dashboard-auto-refresh.md` (`@object-ui/app-shell` patch).

## Zone 2 readings

1. **How a widget re-reads.** The mechanism is the data-invalidation bus. `DatasetWidget`, `ObjectChart`, `ObjectMetricWidget`, `ObjectDataTable`, `ObjectPivotTable` and the filter bar's options each put a `useDataInvalidation` nonce in their fetch effect. `objectName: '*'` is the bus's documented unknown-scope value, and `PageView` already uses it after a page action (`declarePageDataChanged`). The view cannot name its widgets' objects without re-deriving the renderer's widget dispatch: a dataset widget learns its base object only from its query's answer. **Partly falsified in the running console:** a dataset-bound KPI tile never re-reads, because `DatasetWidget` subscribes on the answer's `object`, and the server returns `object` only with drill-through metadata. A direct `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` with no dimensions answered `fields, rows, sql` and no `object`; with a `health` dimension it answered `object: showcase_project`. See Acceptance notes.
2. **The handler.** It is described above. The pin checks that the widget's table node is the same node after each re-read, and the browser run checked the same for all nine widget title nodes.
3. **What the button turns on.** Wiring `onRefresh` shows the renderer's manual refresh button on every console dashboard, whether or not it sets a period. It is small and outlined, with a refresh icon and the label "Refresh All", right-aligned in its own full-width grid row. It sits below any header actions and the filter bar. `hideHeaderText` already hides the renderer's title and description, so the button row does not sit beside a title. For 600 ms after each run, manual or timed, the label reads "Refreshing…", the icon spins and the button is disabled. The renderer's prop doc says `onRefresh` is invoked for "dashboard refresh ... (manual or auto)", so the button is the renderer's contract, not a regression by it. Two costs were measured and declared in the changeset. The row takes one grid row: the first widget's title moved from 306 px to 402 px from the top on the test dashboard. The labels are hard-coded English, and a zh-CN session reads "Refresh All".
4. **Other hosts.** No other host passes `onRefresh`. `DashboardPreview` (the Studio preview and, with `designMode`, the design surface) passes none. That is a source read. `plugin-designer`'s `DashboardEditor` renders its own preview component, not `DashboardRenderer`, also a source read. A `dashboard` node reached through `SchemaRenderer` (the components `page` path) gets no host handler. I measured this with a throwaway probe, not committed: a `dashboard` node with `refreshIntervalSeconds: 60` through the real `SchemaRenderer`, both bare and inside a page region. Each case had 1 dataset read at mount and still 1 after 180 s of fake time, with 0 bus events and no refresh button. A published app page's dashboard therefore ignores the authored period too, which is the same defect in a different host. It is handed to the seat and not changed here.
5. **Pins**, through the real `DashboardView`, `DashboardRenderer`, `DatasetWidget` and bus, under fake timers. Each case counts the adapter's `queryDataset` calls and the bus events:
   - an authored 60 s period re-reads once per period: 1 read at mount, still 1 at 59.999 s, 2 at 60 s and 3 at 120 s, with one `{ objectName: '*' }` event per period and the same table node throughout;
   - `0` and no period each refresh nothing over 180 s;
   - unmounting clears the timer: 1 event at 60 s, still 1 after 180 s more;
   - the manual button re-reads once, in place.
6. **Browser.** See Evidence.
7. **Changeset.** `@object-ui/app-shell` patch. No other package is touched.

## Evidence

The pin's green, red and mutation legs ran on committed trees through `os-verify-lock`. After that leg run, commits `beda3f702` (the test's metadata stub typed instead of cast to `any`) and `a353dcd82` (comments and docs only) followed. Everything else below was re-run on `a353dcd82` unless it names another commit.

- **Pin, green:** `Tests 5 passed (5)`, and it runs inside the app-shell chunk re-run on `a353dcd82`, below.
- **Red leg** at `ae5347527`: `DashboardView.tsx` checked out from base `873284657`. The on-disk blob was `2e95d2a61`, equal to the base blob, and the handler count on disk was 0. Result: `Tests 3 failed | 2 passed (5)`. The period case failed at `the widget was not re-read when the authored period ended` (1 call, expected 2). The unmount case failed at `the timer never ran, so its stop cannot be measured`. The manual case failed because the button is absent. The `0` and absent-period cases pass on base, since they assert absence. Their non-vacuity comes from the period case, which uses the same fixture and differs only in the period. Restore used `git checkout HEAD` on the absolute path inside a trap. Afterwards the blob was `cee18a6e7`, equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` was empty and the status was clean.
- **Mutation leg** at `ae5347527`, through `ablation-replace.mjs`: the handler's scope `'*'` was changed to `'unrelated_object'`. The anchor count went from 1 to 0, and the blob from `cee18a6e76` to `144855f88a`. Result: `Tests 3 failed | 2 passed (5)`, each failing at its re-read count while the bus event still fired. The count assertions are load-bearing on their own. Restore: blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` tests**: 881 test files (`git ls-files`), partitioned into five explicit file lists with no overlap and no remainder, because one run exceeds the foreground cap. At `b671791a0`: `167 passed`, `151 passed`, `184 passed`, `167 passed`, `211 passed | 1 skipped (212)`. The views chunk, which holds the pin and the sibling `DashboardView.*` tests, was re-run at `a353dcd82`: `Test Files 167 passed (167)`, `Tests 1567 passed (1567)`.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-dashboard` tests** (the package is untouched): `Test Files 151 passed (151)`, `Tests 1379 passed | 6 skipped (1385)`.
- **Type-check**: I first built the app-shell dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`, 28 of 28 tasks). Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard run type-check` both exited 0. After `beda3f702`, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exited 0 again, and `--listFiles` includes the new test.
- **eslint** on the two changed source files (`--format json`): 2 files, 0 errors. The test has 0 warnings. `DashboardView.tsx` has 9 warnings, equal to base's 9 (all pre-existing: `no-explicit-any` and one `set-state-in-effect`). This is a declared narrowing. `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting: `parserOptions`, `projectService` and `project:` return zero hits, against a positive control of `react-hooks` with 7 hits. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The package-wide `eslint .` belongs to CI.
- **Gates**, each exit 0 on `a353dcd82`: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`. `check-changeset-claims` pointed at `.changeset/7234-requiredpermissions-author-channel.md`, which names `content/docs/guide/console.md`. That paragraph (the hide, and where the reason is shown) is untouched by the added table row, so it is still true.
- **`scripts/__tests__/`**: I ran the whole directory rather than a hand-derived subset, because the touched docs are in the corpus of many doc gates: `Test Files 177 passed | 2 skipped (179)`, `Tests 5354 passed | 2 skipped (5356)`.
- **Bundle**: no new module is imported. `notifyDataChanged` joins the existing `@object-ui/react` import of `DashboardView`, which `AppContent` loads lazily. `Bundle Analysis` is left to CI.

**Browser**, headless Chromium from `/opt/pw-browsers`. The backend was an objectstack worktree at `542670da` (full `turbo run build`), running `examples/app-showcase` with `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh -p 4062`. The console was this branch's `apps/console` Vite on port 5162, proxied to it. The dashboard was `showcase_ops_dashboard`, with nine dataset widgets. `refreshIntervalSeconds: 10` was saved through `PUT /api/v1/meta/dashboard/showcase_ops_dashboard` (a customization overlay) and read back as 10.

- This branch, with period 10, over a 25 s window: `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` ran 5 times at about 9.3 s and 5 times at about 19.3 s. All nine widget title nodes tagged before the window were the same nodes after it, and the grid node was the same. The sampled button labels were "Refresh All" and "Refreshing…".
- Period 0 (control): 0 dataset queries in 25 s, and the label never read "Refreshing…".
- `main`'s `DashboardView.tsx` with the same period 10: no refresh button and 0 dataset queries in 25 s.
- Out-of-band write: while the page was open, I created a project with `health: red` by REST. That write bypasses the console, so only the timer can surface it. The next timed re-read of "Projects by Health" answered `Red=2`, and the bar repainted. The "At-Risk (Red)" KPI tile still read 1 after 12 s.
- A zh-CN session (the user's `locale` set to `zh-CN`): the shell was in Chinese, and the button read "Refresh All" / "Refreshing…".

## Acceptance notes

- **KPI tiles do not refresh.** Handed to the seat. The 4 of 9 widgets that never re-read are the dataset-bound KPI tiles (no dimensions). `DatasetWidget` keys its bus subscription on the `object` its answer names, and the analytics service attaches `object` only as drill-through metadata. Per the service source, that means only when the selection has a drillable dimension and the answer has at least one row. So such a tile never re-reads on any bus event, whether it is this timer, the button or a declared write. By the same source read, a widget whose first answer was empty never subscribes either. The handler here is not the cause, and nothing in this PR changes `DatasetWidget`. The changeset, README, guide and handler comment all say so.
- **The `'*'` scope reaches other bus readers.** In the browser, the one extra request per period was the signed-in user's language read (`GET /api/v1/data/sys_user/ID`, from `useSignedInUserLocale`). The inbox and approvals polls ran identically with period 0 and on `main`, so they are not this change.
- **The button row costs one grid row** above the widgets: an 80 px track plus a 16 px gap on this positioned grid. This is the renderer's layout, stated in the changeset and not changed here.
- **The page-held dashboard and the untranslated labels** are handed to the seat.
